newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Marks & Spencer opens largest Thai store.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer opens largest Thai store.

text.p: British retailer Marks & Spencer Plc said it opened a new store in Bangkok on Thursday and was looking to expand into another three sites in the Thai capital.

In a statement released in Hong Kong, the company said the 18,000 square foot (1,675 square metre) outlet in Central Plaza Lardprao, its largest in Thailand, would replace a smaller store in the same complex and bring its total retail area in Bangkok to 69,500 square feet.
"With this new store, M&S has now effectively doubled its sales area in Bangkok since July," the statement quoted Paul Smith, regional chief executive, as saying at the opening.
The statement said the company was looking at three new stores, which had the potential to add up to 50,000 square feet of sales space within the next year.
A 30,000-square-foot store in the Chidlom district of central Bangkok was among the projects being considered, the company's Hong Kong office told Reuters.
M&S said it has 35 stores in the Asia-Pacific region, all run as franchises with local partners except eight wholly-owned outlets in Hong Kong.
The company's six franchises in Bangkok are run by Thai department store giant, the Central Group.
